quizzes.question: The northernmost extent of this mountain range includes a region known as the Rif. The rain shadow created by this range contributed heavily to the formation of the Sahara Desert to its south. For the point, name this North African mountain range containing Mount Toubkal, named for a Greek Titan who holds up the sky.
quizzes.explanation: The Atlas Mountains span Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia; their highest peak is Mount Toubkal.

quizzes.question: The Wadi Hadhramaut flows through the arid eastern region of this country, which has no permanent rivers. Its outlying territory of Socotra is famous for endemic species such as the dragon's blood tree. For the point, name this nation on the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula with capitals at Sana'a and Aden.
quizzes.explanation: Yemen is located on the southern Arabian Peninsula and includes the island of Socotra.

quizzes.question: Hypothetical gravity trains have been proposed to travel between pairs of these geographic locations. An uninhabited volcanic archipelago south of Invercargill forms one of these locations opposite to Normandy, France. For the point, name these points situated on exact opposite sides of the Earth from each other.
quizzes.explanation: Antipodes are points on the Earth's surface diametrically opposite to each other.

quizzes.question: Timberline Lodge on the slopes of this peak offers the only year-round ski lift operation in the United States. This mountain features Lolo Pass and was historically known as Wy'east to the Multnomah people. For the point, name this peak in the Cascade Range, the highest mountain in Oregon.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Hood is Oregon's highest peak and home to Timberline Lodge.

quizzes.question: The Presidential Range within this mountain system contains Mount Quincy Adams as well as the site of the former "Old Man of the Mountain" rock formation. A famous rack railway climbs the highest peak of this system, which is notorious for erratic severe weather. For the point, name this mountain range in New Hampshire dominated by Mount Washington.
quizzes.explanation: The White Mountains are a mountain range in New Hampshire containing Mount Washington.

quizzes.question: This city was dubbed the "Paris of the Tropics" during a late 19th-century rubber boom that funded its ornate Teatro Amazonas opera house. It is connected to the town of Iranduba by the Journalist Phelippe Daou Bridge near the Encontro das Águas. For the point, name this major port city located at the confluence of the Rio Negro and Amazon River in northern Brazil.
quizzes.explanation: Manaus is the capital of the Brazilian state of Amazonas, located on the Rio Negro.

quizzes.question: Peaks in this mountain chain, such as Salkantay, were traditionally revered as sacred spirit entities called "Apus." Wild camelid species like the vicuña and guanaco inhabit the high plateaus of this range, which passes near major cities like Quito and Cuenca. For the point, name this longest continental mountain range in the world, running along the western coast of South America.
quizzes.explanation: The Andes stretch over 4,300 miles along South America's western coast.

quizzes.question: Archaeological evidence suggests that the main axis of this site was aligned to face the sunrise on the summer solstice. Located on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, this monument features outer bluestones surrounding massive sarsen stones. For the point, name this prehistoric monument in England featuring a circular arrangement of giant standing stones.
quizzes.explanation: Stonehenge is a famous prehistoric megalithic structure located in Wiltshire, England.

quizzes.question: During a cultural revival in the 1990s, this design was famously worn on a pop art dress by Spice Girl Geri Halliwell. Due to historical maritime ties, the Basque flag was inspired by this emblem, which also forms the canton of national flags like Fiji and Tuvalu. For the point, name this national flag of the United Kingdom.
quizzes.explanation: The Union Jack combines the crosses of St. George, St. Andrew, and St. Patrick to represent the UK.

quizzes.question: By municipal law, modern skyscrapers in this city are prohibited from exceeding the elevation of its central three-peaked hill. Situated at the confluence of the Ottawa and St. Lawrence Rivers, it is the second-largest French-speaking city in the world. For the point, name this most populous city in Quebec, Canada.
quizzes.explanation: Montreal is built around Mount Royal in southwestern Quebec.

quizzes.question: The Journalist Phelippe Daou Bridge connects this city to Iranduba, and it features the Amazon Theatre, which was built during a rubber boom that earned it the nickname "Paris of the Tropics." This city serves as the capital of Amazonas state and lies near the Meeting of Waters between the Solimões River and the Rio Negro. For the point, name this Brazilian city, the largest urban center in the Amazon Basin.
quizzes.explanation: Manaus is the capital of Amazonas, Brazil, located at the confluence of the Rio Negro and Solimões River, known historically for its rubber boom.

quizzes.question: This peak's Lolo Pass was historically used by Native Americans to travel between the Willamette Valley and fishing grounds at Celilo Falls. Known in the Multnomah language as Wy'east, this stratovolcano hosts Timberline Lodge, which offers the only year-round ski resort in the United States. For the point, name this fourth-highest peak in the Cascade Range and the highest mountain in Oregon.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Hood is Oregon's highest peak, located in the Cascade Range and home to Timberline Lodge.

quizzes.question: This island is famous for its endemic dragon's blood tree, Dracaena cinnabari, which features a distinctive umbrella-shaped canopy. Located east of the Horn of Africa near the mouth of the Red Sea, this island lies near the Guardafui Channel in the Indian Ocean. For the point, name this highly biodiverse island that belongs to Yemen.
quizzes.explanation: Socotra is a biodiverse Yemeni island in the Indian Ocean known for unique endemic flora like the dragon's blood tree.

quizzes.question: Mountain peaks in this range, such as Salkantay, are revered in local indigenous traditions as protective mountain spirits called Apus. This mountain system hosts the world's highest active volcano, Ojos del Salado, and borders the high-altitude plateau known as the Altiplano. For the point, name this longest continental mountain range in the world, which runs along the western coast of South America.
quizzes.explanation: The Andes run down the entire western coast of South America and constitute the world's longest continental mountain range.

quizzes.question: This territory's island of Ap Lei Chau is one of the most densely populated places on Earth, and its prominent landmarks include Victoria Peak and the Bank of China Tower. Situated on the eastern side of the Pearl River Estuary, it encompasses the Kowloon Peninsula and New Territories. For the point, name this former British colony that was handed over to China as a Special Administrative Region in 1997.
quizzes.explanation: Hong Kong is a Special Administrative Region of China located on the Pearl River Estuary, handed over from British control in 1997.

quizzes.question: The Gilf Kebir Plateau in this country's Western Desert contains prehistoric cave art, including the famous Cave of Swimmers. This nation contains the low-lying Qattara Depression as well as the Aswan High Dam, which impounds Lake Nasser. For the point, name this North African country containing the Nile River Delta, the city of Luxor, and the Great Pyramids near Cairo.
quizzes.explanation: Egypt is located in North Africa, containing Cairo, the Nile Delta, Lake Nasser behind the Aswan High Dam, and ancient monuments.

quizzes.question: The northernmost section of this mountain range is the coastal Rif region bordering the Alboran Sea. Mount Toubkal in Morocco is the highest summit of this range, which casts a prominent rain shadow contributing to the aridity of the desert to its south. For the point, name this mountain range in northwest Africa named for a mythical Greek Titan.
quizzes.explanation: The Atlas Mountains span Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia in northwest Africa, named after the Titan Atlas.

quizzes.question: This range's northern Presidential section contains Mount Quincy Adams, and it formerly featured a famous natural cliff profile known as the "Old Man of the Mountain." Its peak Tuckerman Ravine is famous for extreme weather conditions and high winds recorded at its summit observatory. For the point, name this mountain range in New Hampshire topped by Mount Washington.
quizzes.explanation: The White Mountains are located in New Hampshire, containing Mount Washington and formerly the Old Man of the Mountain rock formation.

quizzes.question: This island's central region features the Amari Valley, while its northern coast hosts historic Venetian harbors in Chania and Rethymno. Its largest city is Heraklion, which is situated near the ancient archaeological complex of Knossos. For the point, name this largest and most populous Greek island, legendary home of the Minoan civilization.
quizzes.explanation: Crete is the largest Greek island, home to Heraklion and the ancient Minoan palace of Knossos.

quizzes.question: The Benrath and Speyer lines separate dialect divisions of this language, which holds co-official status alongside Italian in the South Tyrol region. Its cultural linguistic sphere, or Sprachraum, includes Liechtenstein and the majority of cantons in Switzerland. For the point, name this West Germanic language spoken predominantly in Austria and Germany.
quizzes.explanation: German is a major West Germanic language spoken in Germany, Austria, parts of Switzerland, and South Tyrol.

quizzes.question: This city is joined to the municipality of Iranduba by the Journalist Phelippe Daou Bridge across the Rio Negro. It contains a monument to the Opening of the Ports, commemorating a late 19th-century rubber boom that gave this city the nickname "Paris of the Tropics." For the point, name this northwestern Brazilian city located at the confluence of the Rio Negro and the Amazon River.
quizzes.explanation: Manaus is the capital of the Brazilian state of Amazonas, famous for its location at the meeting of the waters and its rubber boom history.

quizzes.question: Peaks in this range like Salkantay are regarded as sacred spirits known as Apus in indigenous Quechua tradition. A mountain in this range called El Altar is named for its resemblance to two nuns and four priests, and major high-altitude cities here include Cuenca, Cali, and Quito. For the point, name this longest continental mountain range in the world, dominating western South America.
quizzes.explanation: The Andes run along the entire western coast of South America and host peak Chimborazo, Mount Aconcagua, and major Andean cities.

quizzes.question: The dragon's blood tree Dracaena cinnabari is an iconic species endemic to an archipelago controlled by this nation. Its mainland territory includes the eastern section of the Wadi Hadhramaut and borders the Empty Quarter desert, while lacking any permanent rivers. For the point, name this country on the Arabian Peninsula with its capital at Sana'a and major port of Aden.
quizzes.explanation: Yemen owns the Socotra archipelago (home to the dragon blood tree) and occupies the southwestern corner of the Arabian Peninsula.

quizzes.question: The northernmost ridge of this mountain system is known as the Rif, which runs along the Mediterranean coast. Mount Toubkal is the highest peak in this system, whose rain shadow contributed heavily to the arid climate of the Sahara Desert. For the point, name this North African mountain range extending across Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia, named for a classical titan.
quizzes.explanation: The Atlas Mountains stretch across northwestern Africa and separate the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines from the Sahara Desert.

quizzes.question: The Lolo Pass on this peak historically allowed Native Americans to travel from the Willamette Valley to Celilo Falls. Known as Wy'east to the indigenous Multnomah people, it features Timberline Lodge, which hosts the only year-round ski resort in the United States. For the point, name this dormant stratovolcano in the Cascade Range, the highest peak in the state of Oregon.
quizzes.explanation: Mount Hood is Oregon's tallest mountain (11,249 feet) and is located about 50 miles east-southeast of Portland.

quizzes.question: Carving out jagged sharp ridges called arêtes, these features form shallow kettles as they retreat across a landscape. They transform river-carved V-shaped valleys into broad U-shaped valleys through processes like plucking and abrasion, depositing till into drumlins and moraines. For the point, name these massive, slow-moving bodies of ice that release icebergs into the ocean via calving.
quizzes.explanation: Glaciers reshape terrain through glacial erosion and deposition, leaving distinctive features like moraines, U-shaped valleys, and kettle lakes.

quizzes.question: An isolated island group named after these locations lies 530 miles southeast of Invercargill, New Zealand, and forms one with Normandy, France. Approximate pairings of these locations include Madrid with Wellington, as well as Shanghai with Buenos Aires. For the point, name these geographical points situated on exact opposite sides of the Earth from one another.
quizzes.explanation: Antipodes are points on the Earth's surface diametrically opposite to each other. The Antipodes Islands are named for being antipodal to Great Britain.

quizzes.question: The extremely dense island of Ap Lei Chau is located within this territory, off the southern coast of its primary island. Situated on the eastern side of the Pearl River Estuary, it encompasses the New Territories, Kowloon Peninsula, and Victoria Peak. For the point, name this former British colony that is now a Special Administrative Region of China.
quizzes.explanation: Hong Kong was handed back to China by the UK in 1997 and consists of Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, and the New Territories.

quizzes.question: The remote Gilf Kebir Plateau sits in the hyper-arid Western Desert region of this nation, which also contains the hyper-depressed Qattara Basin. Its major ancient historic sites include the Karnak Temple complex near Luxor and the valley spanned by the Aswan High Dam. For the point, name this northeast African country centered on the lower Nile River, with its capital at Cairo.
quizzes.explanation: Egypt contains iconic geography including the Nile River valley, the Sinai Peninsula, and the Western Desert, alongside historic monuments.

quizzes.question: By municipal ordinance, local skyscrapers are restricted from exceeding the height of this city's central triple-peaked hill. It sits at the confluence of the Ottawa and St. Lawrence Rivers and serves as the northern terminus of Amtrak's Adirondack rail line. For the point, name this most populous city in the province of Quebec, the second-largest city in Canada.
quizzes.explanation: Montreal is named after Mount Royal (Mont Royal), the prominent hill in the city center around which city height limits are regulated.
